content_fields.title: Test that application is not vulnerable to SQL injection
content_fields.description: Replace the interpolated UPDATE with a parameterized statement so no value can alter the query structure.
content_fields.finding: The UPDATE statement is built by f-string interpolation of status_value and order_id and executed through text(), so it is directly injectable.
content_fields.current_code:
raw_sql = f"""
        UPDATE orders 
        SET status = '{status_value}'
        WHERE id = {order_id}
    """
    db.execute(text(raw_sql))
    db.commit()
content_fields.required_fix:
# app/apis/orders/services/get_order_status.py
db_order.status = OrderStatus(delivery_data["status"])
db.add(db_order)
db.commit()

# If raw SQL is genuinely required, bind every value:
# db.execute(
#     text("UPDATE orders SET status = :status WHERE id = :order_id"),
#     {"status": OrderStatus(status_value).value, "order_id": order_id},
# )
criteria: No SQL string in the codebase is built with f-strings, concatenation or % formatting.
The status value is validated against the OrderStatus enum before use.
A delivery response containing `'; DROP TABLE orders; --` leaves the schema intact.
